what: Penalties as Objects with Exact Derivatives
title: Penalties as Objects with Exact Derivatives
text: Penalties regularized Bayesian regression S7 objects. penalty rho(D beta; theta) – linear map, scalar function, hyperparameters – object answers everything estimation routine asks: value normalizing constant, exact derivatives coefficients hyperparameters, mixed block, kink set, , quadratic penalties, rank, null basis log pseudo-determinant marginal criterion consumes. Three branches: quadratic_penalty(); distrib_penalty(), univariate distributions7 log-density applied coordinatewise (ridge_penalty(), lasso_penalty(), heavy_penalty() named instances); scad_penalty() / mcp_penalty(), defined derivative improper construction. Part statmodels7 toolkit.

text: exact negative log-density (possibly degenerate) Gaussian prior \(\beta \sim N(0, (\lambda D'PD)^{-})\): $$\rho = \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,(D\beta)'P(D\beta)   - \tfrac{r}{2}\log\lambda + \tfrac{r}{2}\log 2\pi   - \tfrac{1}{2}\log\mathrm{pdet}(P),$$ \(r\) rank \(P\). constant kept deliberately: dropping , penalized-likelihood software , makes joint hyperparameter estimation degenerate.

title: Construct a Quadratic Penalty — quadratic_penalty
text: One eigendecomposition construction fixes rank relative rule \(\mathrm{ev} > \mathrm{tol}\cdot\max(\mathrm{ev})\) – statement matrix rather whichever arithmetic later performed – stores exact null basis \(D'PD\), membership questions never go rank recomputed assembled sum. Every quantity closed form \(\lambda\).

code: # a second-difference penalty on five coefficients: rank 3, an improper # prior whose null space is the linear polynomials P <- crossprod(diff(diag(5), differences = 2)) pen <- quadratic_penalty(P) penalty_rank(pen) #> [1] 3 is_proper(pen) #> [1] FALSE penalty_value(pen, rnorm(5), list(lambda = 2)) #> [1] 9.451446

what: Construct the SCAD and MCP Penalties — scad_penalty
title: Construct the SCAD and MCP Penalties — scad_penalty
text: SCAD (Fan Li, 2001) defined derivative \(t \ge 0\), $$\rho'(t) = \lambda \;\; (t \le \lambda), \qquad   \rho'(t) = \dfrac{\lambda - t}{- 1} \;\; (\lambda < t \le \lambda),   \qquad \rho'(t) = 0 \;\; (t > \lambda),$$ extended evenly, \(> 2\); MCP (Zhang, 2010) \(\rho'(t) = (\lambda - t/\gamma)_+\) \(\gamma > 1\).
